public_rationale: The accessible Davos interview gives five to ten years, implying approximately 2031–2036. Contemporaneous reporting of Stanford gives 2030 plus or minus a year. These establish the two reported estimates and support calling the January range slower. They do not establish a logical contradiction: both estimates are approximate and overlap in 2031.
limitations: The Davos evidence is a republication of an edited interview; Stanford evidence is reporting rather than a directly retrieved recording transcript.
This assesses the reported timeline comparison, not whether Hassabis’s forecasts were justified or whether Marcus’s description of the precise Stanford week was accurate.

criteria.support_condition: Records of the January Davos interview and the Stanford appearance establish estimates of five to ten years and approximately 2030 plus or minus one year, respectively.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable records show that either attributed estimate was materially different, concerned another milestone, or was not made at the attributed appearance.
